items.note: S2.3 names 'a fixed linear network on W roles' and S2.3.3 alludes to three-element subsets, but no step gives the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, the cancellation of scratch values, or the signed exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

S2.3.1 gives invertible frames with stored array D_v g and says intermediate frames cancel, matching lines 132-143; it omits the reason (the common frame commutes with pointwise gates) and the resulting route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} (eq:common-frame-identity, 814-822).
S2.3.3 alludes to nested subspaces from triple intersections, but gives no labels, no orthogonality of neighbouring triple lines, and none of L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L or L<N/2.

S2.3.2 correctly states that the bit network's endpoint operator is the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D); it omits the matrix assignment with endpoint differences I_m and the edge-rank total s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m that the proposition also asserts.
Only the generic 'both procedures arise from a network with frames' in S2.3 touches it; no step mentions phase frames C_U, translation kernels aI+bX_v, s_c, or the C^{tensor m} endpoint operator.
The plan states s<Wm and s/W<m as the source of the power saving (lines 167-175), but gives neither the reason (L<N/2), the explicit deficits, nor the exponent tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}.

S2.4 says controlled shifts and rational scalings take linear time, in line with the lemmas, but leaves out the conditions (prime radix, b-digit fields, offsets preparable in b^{O(1)}) and the digit-level operations; its quoted line concerns a different point (see errors).
matrix-shear appears only as a page name and dependency; no step states the lower-triangular factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 or that a rank-a shear costs a interchanges plus O(V).

S2.3.4 gives the recursion in prose (s calls at parameter f on volume V/W, ratio s/W<m per factor m), but does not tie it to field digits, nor give the O(1) node overhead, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the W^k row divisibility, or the final three updates completing the interchange.

S2.1 states the O(Vu^tau), tau<1 bound for interchanging two disjoint u-bit address fields of a Cartesian-product array, as in Lemma lem:chunk-swap; it gives no reduction from arbitrary to power widths.

No step concerns the conjugation by P_M, the coordinate kernels C_{e_j}, the s_c child calls of C^{tensor f}, or H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. The generic recursion in S2.3 does not specifically address it.

S2.4 quotes line 177 on whole-chunk moves but omits the controlled-shift additions, the bad set and the deterministic correction of exceptional addresses; no statement of the selected-bit XOR or its cost is given.

The generic recursion of S2.3.4 (s calls on V/W, ratio s/W<m) is the core of F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), but the plan gives neither the node overhead, the leaf cutoff e<d^beta nor the unrolling to d^{lambda'}.

S2.2 states the H_0 layer on one selected bit in up to d chunks at cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), lambda'<1. It omits the exact Gaussian-dyadic evaluation with a single final truncation Q_p and the error bound.

S6 gives the construction (roots of unity are powers of y, root multiplications are signed shifts) and S6.1 the retained frequency order. It omits omega_t=y^{2r/t}, F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the layout L with counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, and the cost and error.

S6.2 rightly says ring products are exact via signed packing and the established multiplier. 'Into one integer' blurs the four evaluation products at B_0=2^{4p} of real and imaginary numerators, and the normalization Q_p(fg/r) and cost O(rp log(rp)) are missing.

S6's method (forward transforms, pointwise product, inverse) with S6.1 (common retained order consumed by the opposite transform) and S6.2 (packed products) follows the paper's route. It lacks the normalization (f*g)/(rM) with its exact scale by M, and the error/cost bounds.

S4 and S4b name resampling through a power-of-two tensor transform with retained permutations. They give no identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, no contractions A,B_0, and no conditions (coprime s<t, theta>p/alpha^4).

S5 names Bluestein's conversion of the middle transform to cyclic convolution and S4b names cancellation, but without the chirp, eq:permuted-chirp or eq:source-permutation-cancel. S4b also mis-assigns cancellation to the target permutation (see errors).
Only kappa=2^{-182} (S0) and 'distinct prime cyclic axes' (S3) appear; there are no sizes b, p=6b, d, K, T, no prime windows, and no fixed exponents.
S3 names a convolution-preserving Chinese-remainder map onto distinct prime axes but does not give Phi: x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, why it is an isomorphism, or its triangular digit form.

S5b faithfully paraphrases line 196-198 (negative wrap gives the cyclic wrap after untwisting) but not the map x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r} or M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g); counted as an allusion without its defining content.

Taken together, the top-level steps give the chain digits -> CRT -> resampling -> chirp -> twist -> synthetic convolution -> recovery. The plan leaves out the source-transform composition 2^gamma B_0 QF_t A, the two forward transforms with pointwise product and opposite transform, and the scales by S and 2^{2b+4}S.
S7 states the decisive inequality (coefficient error <1/2, then rounding and carries give the exact product), as in eq:final-error. The plan gives none of the error chain, p=6b or gamma<=b/4.
S0 states only the final bound O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). There is no cost table, no normalized costs, no margins g_i, and no min g_i=2kappa.
Only the dependency 'nlogn-conjecture' in S0 points to it; no step says how the bound refutes an eventual c_A n lg n lower bound.

errors.says: Source and target permutations stay in the transform identity and cancel instead of being run as sorts.
errors.paper: Only the source permutation R cancels across the two forward transforms, the product and the opposite transform (lines 206-208, eq:source-permutation-cancel). The target permutation Q is absorbed into the middle factor, which Bluestein's identity turns into a cyclic convolution 'including its target permutation' (lines 194-195, eq:permuted-chirp at 3920-3924).

errors.says: Both procedures arise from a fixed linear network; motivation: 'A single network design serves both bit and numerical procedures'.
errors.paper: 'Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network' (line 120): the bit construction over F_2 and the complex construction over Z[i,1/2] have different neighbour rules, wire counts W_b, W_c and call counts s_b, s_c; they share only the eight-row schedule.

errors.says: Arrays on tapes are handled by scans, controlled shifts and rational scalings in linear time, giving the whole-chunk moves the procedures use (quoting line 177).
errors.paper: Line 177 says that changes of numerical address coordinates are implemented by whole-chunk moves and controlled shifts, followed by a deterministic correction of explicitly identified exceptional addresses. Whole-chunk moves are chunk swaps costing O(Vu^tau), not linear-time scans, and the plan drops the correction step.

chain: The plan follows the paper's introduction closely and reaches the main bound along the paper's route: two tape procedures from linear networks with frames and s<Wm, then CRT, resampling, chirp, twist, synthetic convolution and exact recovery. It thins to bare statements almost everywhere. Only the synthetic convolution has a real (partial) derivation, while the finite network construction, both interfaces, the phase-frame recursion, the error chain and the cost table with its margins are only named or absent. It also misstates how the target permutation is removed (S4b).
